Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) or 'n.d.'; partial dates use YYYY or YYYY-MM. verification_status is 'opened' (the page was read during research) or 'listed' (found in a directory or link list, not read). case.name: City of Munich Open Source Program Office
case.local_name: Open Source Hub / OSPO der Landeshauptstadt München

authorizing_act.title: Sitzungsvorlage 20-26 / V 08681, Open Source Hub und Open Source Sabbatical

case.placement: Team within it@M (the city's IT service provider), inside the Competence Center for Software Engineering

headcount.note: Current headcount not published; see gaps.

budget.note: €85,000 is the council figure (V 11273, 2023-11-15); heise reported €75,000 in October 2024.

case.role_in_procurement_detail: Offers procurement consulting (advice, market research on open alternatives, cooperation where no practicable open source solution exists) and is integrated into procurement governance as of April 2024, but states it does not perform tender implementation or make-buy-use-compose analyses. A 2021 council rule requires justification only for in-house development that is not open source. No public exceptions register. A May 2026 coalition agreement made open source the procurement default.
functions: licensing and legal review of city open source releases (MIT default, automated dependency review)
evaluating and prioritizing open source ideas and initiatives
managing the city's presence on public code platforms (GitHub organization it-at-m)
running the Open Source Sabbatical for external developers
sponsoring open source libraries the city depends on
running a biweekly municipal open source community
inter-municipal cooperation via the Municipal Open Source Board (with ZenDiS, KGSt, Dortmund)

key_people.name: Dr. Dirk Gernhardt
key_people.role: Open Source Representative; head of the Competence Center for Software Engineering

key_people.name: Dr. Laura Dornheim
key_people.role: IT commissioner and chief digital officer, political owner

key_people.name: Lars Mentrup
key_people.role: SPD/Volt council member, co-author of the 2020 motions

outcomes_reported.metric: open source applications in city catalogue
savings reported for LiMux desktop migration (EUR)
outcomes_reported.note: City's own figure; disputed by Microsoft-funded studies at the time.

stated_reasons_for_open_source: security through public review of code
legal requirement: Bavarian Digital Act and federal Online Access Act §4

un_principles_mapping.open_by_default: 2021 council priority rule; 2026 coalition default; office advises but does not decide
un_principles_mapping.contribute_back: €85,000/yr sponsorship of upstream libraries; sabbatical program
un_principles_mapping.secure_by_design: stated principle: public code can be checked for security gaps
un_principles_mapping.foster_inclusive_participation: biweekly municipal open source community; sabbatical open to external developers
un_principles_mapping.design_for_reusability: MIT default license; Municipal Open Source Board for inter-city reuse; adopted Berlin's appointment system
un_principles_mapping.provide_documentation: public pages on principles, licenses, sponsoring, sabbatical, repositories
un_principles_mapping.rise: sabbatical; recruitment named as a reason for public code
un_principles_mapping.sustain_and_scale: permanent team and budget line in council decisions; no published metrics on procurement influence

lessons_for_nyc: Copy the founding act: a council decision naming team, host department, headcount and money, plus a second decision for sponsorship.

Write the procurement review role, the options-analysis ownership and a public exceptions register into the founding act; Munich's advisory-only role has needed later political decisions to strengthen.
Extend the justification rule from in-house code to purchased software.
Adopt sponsorship and sabbatical programs as they are.
Publish annual metrics on contracts reviewed, exceptions granted and code released.
